easy.explanation: The KJV says that Jehoash was seven years old when he began to reign.

easy.q: How many years did Jehoash reign in Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: His mother’s name was Zibiah of Beer-sheba.

answers: All his days wherein Jehoiada the priest instructed him
medium.explanation: The KJV connects Jehoash’s right conduct with Jehoiada’s instruction.
medium.q: During what period did Jehoash do what was right in the sight of the LORD?

medium.explanation: The high places were not taken away, and the people continued to sacrifice and burn incense there.
medium.q: What remained active despite Jehoash doing what was right?

answers: Places where people sacrificed and burned incense
Rooms where royal treasures were stored

medium.q: What were the high places in this passage?

answers: Jehoash did not reign in Jerusalem

A young king, right conduct, and active high places

challenge.q: Which combination correctly describes the beginning of Jehoash’s reign?

challenge.q: Which detail is easy to confuse concerning Jehoash’s reign?

short_answers.question: What did the people continue to do in the high places?
short_answers.explanation: The people still sacrificed and burnt incense in the high places.

paragraphs.title: The First Attempt to Repair the Temple

easy.explanation: Jehoash instructed the priests to use the money to repair the breaches of the house of the LORD.
easy.q: Who was instructed to use the money of the dedicated things for repairs?

answers: Repairing the breaches of the house
easy.explanation: The money was intended for repairing the breaches of the house of the LORD.
easy.q: What was the money intended for?

answers: The priests had repaired the house
The Temple had been completely destroyed
The priests had not repaired the breaches of the house
easy.explanation: The KJV says the priests had not repaired the breaches of the house.
easy.q: What was discovered in the twenty-third year of King Jehoash?

answers: Because they had not repaired the breaches of the house
Because they wanted to become kings
medium.explanation: Jehoash asked them why they were not repairing the breaches of the house.
medium.q: Why did King Jehoash call for Jehoiada and the other priests?

answers: He directed the money to be delivered for the repairs
He gave the money to the king of Syria
medium.explanation: He ordered the priests to receive no more money from the people but to deliver it for the breaches of the house.
medium.q: What change did Jehoash make after the repairs had not been completed?

answers: Damaged places in the Temple that needed repair
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the damaged parts of the house of the LORD that needed to be repaired.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “the breaches of the house” mean?

answers: The priests repaired the house, so the offerings were stopped
The money was not being used for the repairs, so the method of handling it was changed
Hazael threatened Jerusalem, so the Temple was rebuilt
challenge.explanation: When the priests had not repaired the house, Jehoash changed the way the money was received and delivered.
challenge.q: Which cause and effect is described in these verses?

answers: They agreed to receive no more money from the people and follow the new arrangement
challenge.explanation: The priests consented to receive no more money from the people and no longer repair the breaches themselves.
challenge.q: What did the priests’ response to the king’s command show?

answers: The command to the priests, failure to repair the house, and a change in how the money was delivered
Failure to repair the house, construction of a chest, and the first command
The new money arrangement, the first command, and then the failure
challenge.explanation: Jehoash first gave instructions to the priests, later learned that the repairs had not been made, and then changed the arrangement.
challenge.q: What is the correct order of events?

short_answers.question: What were the priests told to repair?
short_answers.answer: The breaches of the house of the LORD
short_answers.explanation: The money was intended to repair the damaged places in the Temple.

short_answers.question: In what year had the priests still not repaired the house?
short_answers.answer: The three and twentieth year of King Jehoash
short_answers.explanation: The KJV identifies this as the twenty-third year of his reign.

short_answers.question: What were the priests told to stop receiving?
short_answers.answer: Money from their acquaintances or the people
short_answers.explanation: They were told to receive no more money of their acquaintance and to deliver it for the repairs.

paragraphs.title: The Temple Treasury and Repair Work

answers: A chest with a hole bored in its lid
easy.explanation: Jehoiada took a chest, bored a hole in its lid, and set it beside the altar.
easy.q: What did Jehoiada place beside the altar?

answers: The king of Syria and the princes
The king’s scribe and the high priest

easy.q: To whom was the money given for the Temple work?

answers: To collect all the money brought into the house of the LORD
To provide living quarters for the priests

answers: They were not trusted at all
They did not do the work

The money used to buy timber

short_answers.question: Where was the chest placed?
short_answers.answer: Beside the altar, on the right side as one entered the house of the LORD
short_answers.explanation: Jehoiada set the chest beside the altar on the right side of the entrance.

short_answers.question: Who supervised the counting of the money?
short_answers.answer: The king’s scribe and the high priest
short_answers.explanation: They put the money into bags and counted it.

short_answers.question: Why were the workmen not reckoned with?
short_answers.explanation: The KJV says they were not reckoned with because they dealt faithfully.

paragraphs.title: Hazael’s Threat and the Temple Treasures

easy.explanation: Hazael king of Syria fought against Gath and took it.
Hazael set his face to go up to Jerusalem.
easy.q: Where did Hazael turn after capturing Gath?

answers: The treasures of the house of the LORD and the king’s house
medium.explanation: The gold came from the treasures of the Temple and from the king’s house.
medium.q: From which places was the gold taken?

answers: To persuade him to withdraw from Jerusalem
To appoint him as a priest
medium.explanation: After receiving the treasures, Hazael went away from Jerusalem.
medium.q: What was the apparent purpose of sending the treasures to Hazael?

answers: Places where valuable possessions are stored
medium.explanation: The treasures were places where the Temple and royal wealth were kept.

answers: The capture of Gath created a threat to Jerusalem, so the treasures were sent
The capture of Gath led to the rebuilding of the Temple
There was no connection between the events
challenge.explanation: After taking Gath, Hazael turned toward Jerusalem, and Jehoash sent him the treasures.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between Hazael’s capture of Gath and the sending of the treasures?

answers: The treasures of the Temple and the king’s house
challenge.explanation: Jehoash gave Hazael hallowed things and gold from the Temple and the royal treasury.
challenge.q: What price did Jehoash pay to remove the threat?

answers: Gath was captured, while Jerusalem was spared after the treasures were sent
Jerusalem was captured, while Gath was spared

short_answers.question: What city did Hazael capture?

short_answers.question: Where did Hazael go after receiving the treasures?
short_answers.explanation: The KJV says that Hazael went away from Jerusalem.
